summary: The triage model is performing above its 85% target, but accuracy has fallen from 89% to 87% since a form change, and the two people who understand monthly retraining both leave before the end of December. The retraining scripts sit in a personal cloud workspace with only a six-page README from May, and the replacement engineer cannot start before late February. The model risk committee needs full documentation for sign-off on 20 January, so the pilot is at serious risk of stalling before scaling to all claims by March 2027.

signals.observation: The lead ML engineer, who knows the retraining process, is leaving the project before the January sign-off.
signals.evidence: The lead ML engineer resigned last week, and her last day is 18 December.

signals.observation: The contractor who built the feature pipeline leaves at year end and cannot be extended under procurement rules.
signals.evidence: The data engineer who built the feature pipeline is a contractor whose contract ends on 31 December and cannot be extended under procurement rules.

signals.observation: Monthly retraining depends on undocumented knowledge and scripts held in a personal workspace, known only to the two departing people.
signals.evidence: These two are the only people who know how the monthly retraining works. It runs from scripts in the lead engineer's personal cloud workspace, and the only documentation is a six-page README last updated in May.

signals.observation: Model accuracy is declining, and the cause has been linked to a change in the claim form.
signals.evidence: Accuracy has dropped from 89% to 87% over two months, since a change to the online claim form.

signals.observation: No replacement is in place, and the earliest realistic start is late February, after the sign-off date.
signals.evidence: The replacement role has been open three weeks with four applicants, and the earliest realistic start is late February.

signals.observation: The risk committee sign-off requires full model documentation, which does not currently exist in usable form.
signals.evidence: The internal model risk committee's validation sign-off is scheduled for 20 January. The risk committee requires full model documentation before sign-off.

signals.observation: The plan to scale to all claims by March 2027 depends on sign-off and a stable retraining process, both now at risk.
signals.evidence: The plan is to scale to all claims by the end of March 2027.

things_to_watch: Whether the retraining scripts can be moved out of the personal cloud workspace and into controlled storage before 18 December.
Who will hold access and credentials to the scripts and data pipeline after the two leavers depart.
Whether a knowledge transfer or handover session can be scheduled before 31 December, and who will run it.
Whether the 20 January sign-off date can be kept if the documentation is not complete.
Cause of the accuracy drop from 89% to 87% and whether it continues to fall after the form change.
Whether the next monthly retraining run is due before the replacement starts and who will run it.
Options for interim contract or consultant cover, given the contractor cannot be extended.
The cost and timing of the scale-up from 15% to all claims, and whether the March 2027 date is still realistic.
